reason: At base the object JIT fastpass keeps the value written alongside a swallowed issue, so safeParse({}) yields data with an 'a' key set to 'leaked'; the test requires no key at all.
The fix guards both the issue concat and the assignment on !issues.length || present, so an absent optional key produces no key in the output while a present failing key still errors.
Before the fix the paragraph continuation lookahead only treated space-only lines as blank, so a tab-only middle line is swallowed as lazy continuation and both texts merge into one paragraph.
The widened [ \t]+\n lookahead makes a tab-only line count as blank, so the two texts render as two separate paragraph elements.
The change only touches error-path stack decoration; default JSON response transformation is untouched, so a 200 application/json response still resolves with a parsed object at base.
Default response transform still parses JSON into an object; the stack-decoration hardening does not affect the success path.
Parsing a plain boolean flag such as --verbose is unrelated to the negative-number exponent regex, so it works at base.
Adding case-insensitive exponent matching to the negative-number detector does not affect ordinary boolean flag parsing.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt goes straight to JsonPrimitive.getAsInt, and Integer.parseInt accepts full-width Unicode digits, so the conversion silently yields 123 instead of raising a parse error.
The added validateAscii check in JsonTreeReader.nextInt throws MalformedJsonException for the full-width digit string, matching the expected clear parsing error.
The base regex [a-zA-z0-9$]+ splits 'test-db' at the hyphen, producing set search_path to "test", "db" instead of the single schema name.
The new delimiter blocklist regex [^\s,"']+ keeps 'test-db' intact, so the search path is set to the single quoted schema name.
Transformations are allowed by default in request options; the PR only changes ByteBufferUtil pool-buffer recycling, which is unrelated to this behaviour.
The buffer-leak fix does not touch transformation option handling, so the default isTransformationAllowed behaviour still applies the center-crop.
At base allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics is computed on demand from the configured allowed_symbols, so an identifier using only alphanumerics plus an allowed symbol reports no violation.
Applying allowed_symbols from configuration mutates the property, firing the new didSet that refreshes the cached character set, so the allowed symbol is still accepted.
The PR only adds a <cstdint> include, so behaviour is unchanged; node-canvas does not percent-decode non-base64 data URI payloads before handing them to the SVG parser, so the image fails to load.
Arrow's shift adds a relativedelta in wall-clock terms, giving 2025-03-09T04:30:00-05:00 rather than the expected 05:30; the Afrikaans locale change is unrelated.
Adding the <cstdint> include is a compile-only fix and does not add percent-decoding of data URI payloads, so the encoded SVG data URI still fails to load.
Vapor's content decoding rejects a request with no body (422 Unprocessable Entity) even when all properties are optional, and the cookie-header PR does not change that.
The Cookie header parsing change is unrelated to content decoding; an empty form-urlencoded body still produces a 422 rather than an all-nil decoded value.
Afero's MemMapFs.Remove deletes the entry without checking for children, so it returns nil instead of a 'directory not empty' error; the spelling-only PR changes nothing.
The PR only fixes typos, so MemMapFs.Remove still removes a non-empty directory without returning an error.
The Comparator's index rename detection hits an undefined array key when one removed index has two equally matching added candidates; the json_encode flags PR does not touch it.
Fixing the json_encode depth/flags argument in a test does not change Comparator behaviour, so the undefined array key warning during ambiguous index rename detection remains.
shift(hours=10) performs wall-clock arithmetic, yielding 2025-03-09T04:30:00-05:00, not the expected 05:30-05:00; the Afrikaans locale addition is unrelated.

Lowering limitForPeriod below the available permits makes the SemaphoreBasedRateLimiter refresh task throw, which cancels the scheduled task; the CircuitBreaker predicate fix does not affect the rate limiter.
The CircuitBreaker permit-leak fix is unrelated to the rate limiter, so the refresh task still dies once the limit is lowered below available permits and admissions stop.

The PR only touches prefer-template's fixer, so no-var's autofix behaviour is unchanged; rewriting the var to a block-scoped declaration makes the earlier call of the nested function throw a ReferenceError instead of logging undefined.
The prefer-template ASI fix does not change no-var's autofix, which still converts the var to let and makes the indirectly invoked function throw a ReferenceError rather than printing undefined.
The log-formatter adapter change is unrelated to job persistence; SitemapSpider with JOBDIR does not resume its remaining sitemap URLs and the resumed run finishes having crawled nothing.
Fixing logformatter_adapter has no effect on JOBDIR resumption, so the restarted sitemap spider still fails to continue the remaining URLs.
The PR only widens --sanitize's bidi detection; the highlighted-background rendering at --terminal-width 1 with a double-width character still panics with a capacity error.
The bidi-control sanitize fix does not touch the wrapping/highlight code path, so bat still aborts with a capacity overflow at terminal width 1 for a double-width character.
The syslog RFC5424 regex optimization is unrelated; the file output plugin updates the symlink only for one chunk per flush, so only one of the two key-specific symlinks appears.
Changing the structured-data regex has no effect on out_file symlink handling, which still creates a symlink for only one of the distinct chunk keys in the batch.

HikariCP generates the default pool name inside synchronized (System.getProperties()), so construction can block on unrelated system-property access; the ConcurrentBag virtual-thread change does not alter that.
The ConcurrentBag yield/park change is unrelated to pool-name generation, which still synchronizes on the JVM-wide System.getProperties() object.
The SORT ACL keyspec fix is unrelated to persistence; the described 32-bit background-save scenario is a known failure mode, so the save does not report success at this revision.
The ACL/SORT change cannot affect RDB background saving, so the 32-bit server still fails the background save instead of logging 'terminated successfully'.
CTRL-A parses the number into a 64-bit integer, so a 47-digit value overflows and the line is rewritten with altered digits; the CWD/context PR is unrelated.
CTRL-X uses the same 64-bit number parsing, so the oversized number is mangled rather than decremented digit-for-digit, and the nvim_win_set_buf CWD fix is unrelated.
With an untyped NULL the || operator does not resolve to list concatenation, so the result is not typed INTEGER[]; the external file cache race fix is unrelated.
typeof([1] || NULL) does not report a list type while list_concat does, and the file-cache RetireBlocks change does not touch operator binding.
Reading a member of a RefCounted instance from _notification(NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE) in GDScript is the known crash scenario; the ScrollBar touch-input PR does not affect it.
The ScrollBar drag-scrolling change is unrelated to RefCounted predelete notification handling, which still misbehaves when the script accesses the dying object.
f_regression divides by the zero norm of a constant column, producing NaN and a RuntimeWarning rather than F=0.0 and p=1.0; the decision-tree categorical/absolute_error check is unrelated.
r_regression computes sqrt of a slightly negative centered norm for a near-constant column, emitting a RuntimeWarning and NaN; the tree criterion validation PR does not change this.
The Swagger UI readonly fix is unrelated, and Vault Agent's file sink does not end up applying the configured octal mode to the token file.
The UI-only swagger change cannot affect the agent file sink, whose written token file does not carry the configured mode bits.
With no usage placeholder and no parameters, write_usage is called with empty args, and at base wrap_text('') discards the prefix so only a blank line is emitted instead of 'Usage: cli'.
The new empty-args branch writes the prefix with the trailing space stripped, so the first help line is exactly 'Usage: cli'.
Returning a dict from a view is converted to a compact application/json response; the IPv6 partition fix in run()/test client is unrelated.
The urlsplit change only affects host/port parsing for the dev server and test client cookies, so dict-to-JSON view responses behave as before.
Missing-required-field validation is core pydantic behaviour and is unaffected by the deprecated-alias lookup change.
Using id()-keyed deprecated aliases during schema generation does not change required-field validation, which still raises a missing error.
logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same value, so the default effective level already suppresses INFO SQL echo at base and echo=True still logs.
Renaming the constant to logging.WARNING is behaviour-neutral, so echo-off suppresses SQL logging and echo-on logs the statement.

At base method_missing short-circuits when attribute methods are already generated and falls through to the ActiveModel lookup, so reading the aliased value stays within a small multiple of a real column read.

The thread-safe rewrite makes every method_missing call run define_attribute_methods and public_instance_method, raising and rescuing a NameError for a non-column alias, which pushes the access-time ratio well past 20x.
At base each dispatch pushes a new WrappedListener onto the callStack, so getCalledListeners returns one entry per invocation, i.e. two after two dispatches.
The fix stores called listeners in a deduplicated per-event list, so after two dispatches with one listener getCalledListeners reports only one entry instead of two.
Cobra's generated script tracks last_command and clears COMPREPLY at init, so each subcommand's custom completion hook returns its own scoped suggestions.
Replacing the COMPREPLY command substitution with a read loop keeps the same reply contents, and COMPREPLY is reset at completion start, so per-subcommand hooks still yield their own values.
qs combines repeated bare keys into an array regardless of count (arrayLimit only affects explicit numeric indices), so 25 repeats of ids parse to a 25-element array at qs 6.13.0.
qs 6.14.0 keeps the same handling of repeated bare keys, so the parsed ids value remains an ordered 25-element array.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only url, so calling it with a single argument returns the proxy dict without error.
The PR changes the signature to get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) with no default, so a single-argument call raises TypeError for the missing argument.
At base parse_unit_value bails out unless the token starts with a digit or -digit, so '.foons' is never treated as a unit value and parses as a plain string.
Allowing a leading '.' makes '.foons' enter unit-value parsing (it ends with the ns unit) where '.foo' is not a valid number, producing a parse error instead of the string.
At base a sink/CURLOPT_FILE is still attached for HEAD requests, which combined with Accept-Encoding is the reported failure the PR fixes.
After the change no sink or write target is connected for HEAD requests, so the request with Accept-Encoding completes and returns a response.
At base maps are left as values and inspected, and inspect handles the improper list fine, so the assertion fails with a normal match error and no formatting crash.
Converting maps to AST means the improper list [1 | 2] is walked by the AST/algebra formatter, which cannot handle an improper list, so formatting the failure crashes.
At base css_props registers a teardown that removes the wrapper element, so after the dynamic outer component is swapped the inner component loses the --prop wrapper and the text is no longer red.
Removing the element-removal teardown and unifying the dynamic-component codegen keeps the css-props wrapper in place, so the inner component stays red after the toggle.
At base the plugin only requires the code to contain 'new URL' and 'import.meta.url', and the matching regex uses \s, so a multi-line call is transformed and the asset is emitted.
The new code filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ has no dotAll flag, so a call split across lines never matches and the transform is skipped, leaving the asset unemitted.
At base no item text is exported into the child environment, so a NUL-containing item does not affect launching the preview command.
Exporting FZF_CURRENT_ITEM with the raw item text puts a NUL byte in an environment variable, which makes the preview child process fail to start.
At base EDGE_TO_EDGE sets the layout-only flags through setSystemUiVisibility, clearing the immersive-sticky hide flags so the system bars reappear.

The new EDGE_TO_EDGE branch returns after calling WindowCompat without updating mEnabledOverlays/setSystemUiVisibility, so the previously applied immersive-sticky hide flags remain and the bars stay hidden.
At base there is no multiple-case-assignment check, so a class pattern keyword binding the same name reports no syntax error.
The new visitor inserts the class-pattern keyword name and then the name bound by its sub-pattern, so num_classes=num_classes is falsely flagged as a duplicate assignment.
At base the value-slice branch indexes sli.Index(i) without growing the slice, so decoding two blocks into a one-element slice panics with an index out of range.
The added append grows the destination slice when i exceeds its length, so both blocks decode and the field ends up with two entries.
At base the mocked instance is only converted when an explicit timezone is passed, so now() reports the mocked moment in America/Los_Angeles instead of the default UTC.
The fix falls back to date_default_timezone_get(), so the mocked now is presented in the application's default UTC timezone as expected.
The base regex /^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/ requires exactly two leading slashes followed by a non-slash, so '///test.com', '/\t//test.com' and '/\\/test.com' are not classified as protocol-relative.
The widened regex /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/ matches three or more slashes, interleaved whitespace and mixed slash forms, so all three inputs are protocol-relative.
MD5 of 'abc' is unaffected by switching combineOrdered/combineUnordered to the internal byte accessor, so the digest is the standard value.
The change is a copy-avoiding micro-optimization in hash combining and does not alter Hashing.md5() output.
Generating a client for an interface with a GET attribute works at base; the diagnostics refactor is unrelated to code generation output.
Moving diagnostic descriptors to a dedicated class keeps codes, messages and generated code identical, so the generated client still issues the expected GET.
A simple HTTP/1.1 GET with a Content-Length body works at base; the removed continue statements are in unrelated frame-discard and h2 paths.
Dropping the redundant continue statements does not change control flow, so the plain HTTP/1.1 response body is still read correctly.
At base to_iso8601/2 converts to the ISO calendar and then calls to_iso8601/1, dropping the requested :basic format, so the non-ISO date renders as '2001-01-01'.
The fix forwards the format to to_iso8601/2 after conversion, so the basic form '20010101' is returned for the custom-calendar date.
On PHP 8.2+ the native end property cannot be written after construction, so at base it still shows 2024-09-30 after setEndDate even though getEndDate returns the new value.
syncNativePeriod re-initializes the parent DatePeriod after setEndDate, so both the end property and getEndDate report 2025-06-15.
At base no whitespace validation exists, so the request line with the embedded newline is built and sent instead of raising an invalid-URI error.
The added match?(/\s/) checks raise HTTP::RequestError for the newline-containing path before anything is transmitted.
English number-to-words output is independent of the Albanian locale file, so 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 render as 'one million' and 'two million' at base.
Adding an Albanian pluralName does not affect the default English locale conversions.
Singleton scope resolution is unrelated to the Properties loading cast, so both resolutions return the same instance at base.
Filtering non-String property keys does not change single/singleton definition resolution, which still returns the identical instance.
At base replaceElement appends, swaps and removes the last element, yielding ('a',1),('z',2),('c',3), and the duplicate-key precondition already rejects an existing key.
The shared _replaceNew primitive plus in-place value exchange produces the same ordering and result, and the duplicate-key precondition is retained.
At base the negative parsed size is explicitly clamped to zero before multiplication, so '-5MB' yields 0.
max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is equivalent to the removed clamp, so '-5MB' still returns 0.
At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec indexes children[0] (a static child) for the wildcard, hits the default case and panics with 'invalid node type' before the mis-cased /PREFIX/XXX path can resolve.
The fix walks static children via indices and falls back to the wildcard child at the end, so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx and unmatched paths return not-found without a panic.
At base toBigInt returns the nil Int on Exp==0 and IsInt64 dereferences it, so a valid Numeric with a nil Int panics in Int64Value instead of returning zero.
The guard returns big.NewInt(0) when Int is nil, so the valid-but-empty Numeric converts to 0 for both Float64Value and Int64Value without panicking.
The change only adjusts renderer tab-stop handling; external Quit still returns the run loop promptly, which is already the base behavior.
Renderer tab-stop restoration does not affect program shutdown via an externally-invoked Quit, so the run call still returns cleanly.
At base run_until_cancelled polls the wrapped future before checking cancellation, so the already-cancelled token still polls (and thus the panic!-ing future is executed) instead of returning None.
The early is_cancelled() check returns None without polling, so the inner operation is never started and no panic occurs.
The change concerns skipping unreachable .ignore files during directory walking; case-insensitive search matching is unaffected, so matches are still found regardless of letter case at base.
Ignore-file loading optimization does not touch case-insensitive pattern matching, so all case variants are still reported as matches.
The original nested condition already sets Default::Default for skip_deserializing fields with no container default, so the omitted field receives its type default at base.
The refactor keeps the identical condition (container_default none and skip_deserializing set implies Default::Default), so behavior is unchanged and the field still defaults.
